title: Jev feature comparison

features.title: Text state
features.definition: Accept natural-language state directly.

features.title: JSON state
features.definition: Accept objects/arrays directly, preserving their content in model input.

features.title: Structured instructions
features.definition: Accept object/array instructions, not only a string.

features.title: Structured criteria
features.definition: Accept object/array option or level descriptions.

features.title: Custom yes/no criteria
features.definition: Describe what true and false mean in a Noul question.

features.title: Other languages
features.definition: Non-English input is supported or documented; equal accuracy is not implied.

features.title: Image input
features.definition: Decision path consumes image content directly, beyond OCR/text preprocessing.

features.title: Audio/video input
features.definition: Decision path directly accepts audio or video.

features.title: Choice
features.definition: Select a member of a runtime-defined answer set.

features.title: Score expectation
features.definition: Return the probability-weighted index of ordered rubric levels.

features.title: Noul
features.definition: Return a native yes-probability field for a binary question.

features.title: Full probabilities
features.definition: Expose a probability for every choice or level.

features.title: Confidence field
features.definition: Return a separate scalar confidence/concentration measure. Formulas may differ.

features.title: Score legend
features.definition: Return level-index-to-description mapping with an ordinal score.

features.title: Constrained answers
features.definition: Construct the decision from declared options or numeric values; no generated-answer parsing.

features.title: Runtime answer sets
features.definition: Options/rubrics can change per request without retraining a fixed-label classifier.

features.title: Multiple questions
features.definition: An exposed interface accepts multiple decisions in one invocation.

features.title: Mixed question types
features.definition: Choice, Score and Noul can be requested together.

features.title: Parallel questions
features.definition: Questions are evaluated together, rather than a serial question loop.

features.title: Question isolation
features.definition: Another question does not become context for this question. Sequential independent calls count.

features.title: Encode state once
features.definition: Reuse model state computation across questions. Reusing tokenization alone does not count.

features.title: No text decoding
features.definition: Decision inference has no autoregressive answer-generation loop. Not necessarily one backbone call.

features.title: Question IDs ignored
features.definition: Question IDs are response metadata, not model-visible instructions.

features.title: Decision-specific training
features.definition: Weights or adapters are trained for bounded decision outputs.

features.title: Calibration method
features.definition: An explicit method targets probability calibration; this is not an accuracy guarantee.

features.title: Calibration-oriented RL
features.definition: An RL objective includes probability/calibration incentives. Independent methods are not exact Jev RLCD.

features.title: Fitted temperature
features.definition: A fitted temperature is supplied or a fitting method is present; a user-set scalar alone is insufficient.

features.title: User fine-tuning
features.definition: The inspected project exposes model adaptation with user data; service-specific for Jev.

features.title: 255 choices
features.definition: An individual decision supports Jev's 255-option cardinality. Variable-size heads alone are only partial evidence.

features.title: 10 score levels
features.definition: Native Score accepts ten ordered levels.

features.title: 32k state + question
features.definition: Direct model input accepts a 32k-token state-plus-question branch; chunking does not count.

features.title: 64k total request
features.definition: One multi-question request supports Jev's 64k total-input contract.

features.title: Free-text generation
features.definition: The inspected decision interface generates arbitrary answer text.

features.title: SystemOne HTTP route
features.definition: A local/service POST /v1/systemone endpoint exists. Exact wire parity is not implied.

features.title: Model/version selection
features.definition: Select or pin the model/checkpoint used. This is broader than Jev's alias API.

features.title: Token usage
features.definition: Decision results expose input/output token accounting; semantics may differ.

features.title: Python interface
features.definition: A Python client or callable model/scorer interface is supplied.

features.title: JS/TS package
features.definition: A dedicated JavaScript/TypeScript package is supplied; generic HTTP access is not counted.

features.title: Local weights
features.definition: Public model weights/adapters can be used locally. Download/installation status is irrelevant.

features.title: Published low latency
features.definition: Provider latency claim, not a controlled cross-project benchmark.

features.title: Input-token pricing
features.definition: Hosted input-token charge. Local compute cost is a different quantity.

features.title: Free output tokens
features.definition: Hosted billing policy, separate from whether inference generates text.

features.title: Published rate limits
features.definition: Hosted account quotas, not model throughput.

features.title: No training on requests
features.definition: Provider commitment about customer requests/responses; not inferred from local execution.

features.title: Enterprise ZDR
features.definition: An enterprise zero-data-retention service offering.

notes: Scope: the documented Jev 1.13 model/API feature surface, limits and service terms. Undisclosed internals cannot be inventoried. SDK retry/error conveniences are grouped under the client interfaces.

Yes means implemented or officially documented at the inspected revision, not benchmarked here. Partial means a different interface, narrower path, or qualified support. Unknown means the available evidence is insufficient. No is scoped to the inspected decision path.

The comparison does not score project maturity. A missing response wrapper and a missing learned capability are different gaps; comments distinguish them. Ballot, Jevlike, Cua-S1 and SemIf must not be treated as full Jev wire-format implementations merely because they score options.

Confidence is a distribution-derived convenience statistic. Jev does not publicly specify an exact universal formula here. The alternatives use different statistics; thresholds are not interchangeable. Nagi Big supplies a temperature, while Huge/Enormous explicitly use 1.0.

Shared state means reused model computation across questions. Laya reuses tokenization, Ballot batches option encodings, and daseinlabs caches a prefix across options; these are different from Jev/Kev/SemIf shared-question computation.

Calibration-oriented RL is not an exact-RLCD-reproduction claim. Laya implements a logit-noise reward objective. Cua-S1 calibrates an episode-confidence quantity. Neither establishes TypeSafe algorithm equivalence.

Native primitives support composed patterns such as routing, scoring, filtering, reranking, verification, bounded extraction, function/argument selection, taxonomy traversal and downstream feature generation. Those require application code and are not independent built-in model tools.

No cross-project accuracy, speed, language, context-length or calibration benchmark was run. Service prices/quotas are a dated snapshot and do not measure architectural alignment. Public weights were not all downloaded.
